data.text: OPERATOR ANSWERS (2026-10-22): Q1/Q2: adopt the request/approve/consume protocol for every gated command; relayed consent (--yes --reason on upgrade, plan confirm, skew override) kept for ONE more release as a stated time-boxed exception, doctor warns on each use, then per-verb require_approval turns on (recommended). Q3/Q4: operator chose "Terminal + chat/PR approvals" (NOT the recommended terminal + signed): MVP channels are CLI (L1, usable remotely over ssh) plus chat/PR approvals (Slack/Linear/GitHub through the existing connectors). RA-channel-chat moves INTO the minimal path; RA-channel-signed stays queued but later and optional. The operator did not answer the SSH/FIDO2 key part of Q4. Chat/PR approvals are forgeable if the agent holds the connector/gh token; doctor must say it. Q5/Q6: operator chose "Accept harness answers for T2 now": the transcript-attested AskUserQuestion answer is accepted as an L2 channel for T2 (enabled by default), T2 only, never T3. Q6 minimum levels: T2 any person channel (L1/L2/L3), T3 L4 only, single-uid host T3 rated no stronger than L1 with doctor saying so (recommended, unchanged). Q7: gated acts beyond today refusals: complete --force and claim --force only. Q8: operator ticked three example rules (extra review round up to 5 per item/gate when tree changed after triage; skip of a gate whose reviewer was unavailable 3 times; accept a measured baseline-red ci partial) AND ticked "ship none as examples" (contradictory). Q9/Q12: request lives 24h (ask_ttl_s), use window 1h, one use; auto_request on refusal = yes. Q10/Q11: brief/status/inbox notification now; push when AW-sinks lands (never to a channel the agent can read for one-time codes); a serve host the agent cannot reach is NOT in this phase (upgrade path via P-remote.*).

data.alternatives: Trusting the model's statement that the operator agreed (indistinguishable from injection); a second engine (violates r-reuse-core); weakening refusals.
data.consequences: Each refusal site gains a route message; ask verdict stops trusting self-reported human/coded flags above L1; same-uid forgery of L1-L3 stays possible and is stated, not hidden.
data.context: Operator 2026-10-22: manage everything remotely, automated and safe; agent runs gated commands with permission.
data.decision: Yes. Every operator-gated command becomes runnable by an agent with a recorded, single-use, expiring, command-bound approval (D-RA-1), on the existing services/ask engine.
data.title: Adopt request/approve/consume on the ask engine for every gated command

data.alternatives: Require --approval at once (breaks unattended flows); keep relayed consent forever (leaves the injection hole).
data.consequences: A release-bound exception that must be removed: RA-consume records the release and the require_approval default flip as a dated task; doctor warning is mandatory, not optional. D-RA-2 applies to every other gated command immediately.
data.context: Do not break unattended flows while the new path lands.
data.decision: Relayed consent (--yes --reason on upgrade, plan confirm, skew override) is accepted for ONE more release as a stated, time-boxed exception to D-RA-2 for these verbs only; doctor warns on each relayed use. After that release, per-verb require_approval switches on.
data.title: Relayed consent kept one more release as a time-boxed exception, then require_approval per verb

data.alternatives: Recommended CLI + signed MVP: needs a key the operator does not want to manage first.
data.consequences: HONEST LIMIT: chat/PR approvals are forgeable if the agent holds the connector or gh token (research rating stands); doctor must say so and rate L3 accordingly when the agent can read/post with that credential. T3 stays unreachable until a signed channel exists, so T3 acts remain terminal-only (L1 rated per D-RA-Q6) in the meantime.
data.context: Operator works remotely and wants to approve from chat or a PR rather than hold a signing key.
data.decision: Operator chose 'Terminal + chat/PR approvals' over the recommended terminal + signed. MVP channels: CLI (L1, usable remotely over ssh) and chat/PR approvals (Slack/Linear/GitHub via existing connectors) as L3. RA-channel-chat moves into the minimal path; RA-channel-signed stays queued, later, optional. Harness (L2) per D-RA-Q5.
data.title: MVP channels: CLI (L1) plus chat/PR approvals (L3); signed (L4) later and optional

data.alternatives: Asking again now (blocks nothing on the MVP); ddflow-managed keys (custody in the adversary's reach).
data.consequences: Until answered, T3 has no real protection and doctor says 'no approval signer pinned'.
data.context: Q4 not answered; signed channel deferred by D-RA-Q3.
data.decision: The operator did not answer the SSH/FIDO2 key question. When RA-channel-signed is built the recommended default applies: [approvals].signers is a digest-pinned signer list held outside the repo (operator's one out-of-band act), may fall back to the commit allowed-signers file when unset, and ddflow never creates or stores keys (D-CM-7). Recorded as UNANSWERED: ask again before RA-channel-signed is claimed.
data.title: Signed channel signer list: recommended default kept; operator did not answer (UNANSWERED)

data.alternatives: Off by default, opt-in per verb (recommended): rejected by the operator for friction.
data.consequences: CAVEATS: the answer reaches ddflow only through the model/transcript; weak outside local sessions; cloud sessions need RA-probe-harness first (channel inert there until the probe passes). RA-channel-harness must implement attestation so an agent-typed claim of an answer is refused; adversarial tests in RA-e2e cover it. Doctor reports the channel as enabled and its limits.
data.decision: Operator chose 'Accept harness answers for T2 now': the transcript-attested AskUserQuestion answer is an L2 channel for T2, enabled by default (not off), T2 only, never T3. Acceptance must be verifiable via the hook/transcript attestation design (ddflow reads the harness-produced record), never the agent's word.
data.title: Transcript-attested AskUserQuestion answer accepted as L2 for T2, enabled by default

data.alternatives: L1-only for T3 (no real top tier).
data.consequences: With signed deferred (D-RA-Q3) T3 acts are effectively unreachable by agents until RA-channel-signed lands; that is the safe direction.
data.context: A forgeable level must never enroll or rotate its own signer.
data.decision: T2 accepts any person channel (L1, L2, L3). T3 requires L4 only. On a single-uid host whose signer pin is in an agent-writable layer, T3 is rated no stronger than L1 and doctor says so. Signer pin anchored where the agent cannot write when one exists, else the user layer; doctor flags 'no approval signer pinned'.
data.title: Minimum level per tier: T2 any person channel, T3 L4 only; single-uid T3 rated as L1

data.consequences: RA-inventory lists exactly these two new sites; its test fails if another appears unlisted.
data.context: They already have a hook/flag guard.
data.decision: T2 acts added: the override form of complete and the override form of claim (the two forcing flags). cleanup --apply, version cut, promote, decision supersede stay ungated.
data.title: Gated acts beyond today's refusals: forced complete and forced claim only

data.alternatives: Ship none (drops the examples); ship enabled (not what either tick means).
data.consequences: If the lead confirms 'none', delete the example rules from RA-policy; nothing runs meanwhile because they are off.
data.context: Contradictory answer; chose the reading that is safe under both (off by default).
data.decision: Ship three example rules, ALL OFF by default, each reported when enabled and each use reported: (1) extra review round up to 5 per item/gate when the tree changed after triage; (2) skip of a gate whose reviewer was unavailable 3 times; (3) accept a measured baseline-red ci partial. AMBIGUOUS: the operator ticked all three AND 'ship none as examples'; the lead should confirm later.
data.title: Standing auto-approval example rules: three shipped, all OFF (operator answer ambiguous)

data.consequences: Both are knobs under [approvals] (r-everything-configurable); expiry is an event (D-RA-5).
data.context: Short use window limits stale approvals.
data.decision: Request lives 24h (existing ask_ttl_s); an approval is usable 1h after the answer; one use (counted bundles up to [grants].max_count).
data.title: Windows: request 24h, use window 1h, one use

data.consequences: With chat approvals in MVP (D-RA-Q3), one-time codes may only go to a sink the agent cannot read; doctor flags otherwise.
data.context: Push to an agent-readable channel weakens the code.
data.decision: Notify via brief/status/inbox now; push when AW-sinks lands, and never to a channel the agent can read for one-time codes.
data.title: Pending-request notification: brief/status/inbox now, push when AW-sinks lands

data.consequences: Same-uid forgery of L1-L3 remains until then; docs say so.
data.decision: Not in P-remote-approvals; documented as the upgrade path via P-remote.*.
data.title: A serve host the agent cannot reach is out of this phase

data.consequences: Spam is bounded by dedup on digest and the 24h expiry.
data.decision: [approvals].auto_request = true: the refusal site files the request automatically.
data.title: Auto-request on refusal

Optional. Code delivered through an AW-sinks sink the agent cannot read; the forge reply verified through infra/forge with an approver allow-list and reviewer != author. Documents that an agent holding the operator's connector or gh token can forge it. (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22 (D-RA-Q3): MVP channel, not optional. Doctor must state that chat/PR approvals are forgeable if the agent holds the connector/gh token; one-time codes never go to a channel the agent can read (D-RA-Q10).
data.title: Chat and forge approvals (one-time code over a sink; GitHub PR review or /approve by a named login) as L3; MVP channel with the CLI (D-RA-Q3)

data.body:
approvals show --sign-payload prints the payload (namespace ddflow-approval; ask id, digest, outcome, expiry); approve --signature verifies and records the answer; the agent may courier it. ddflow never creates or stores a key (D-CM-7). Falls back to the commit allowed-signers file. If ssh-keygen is missing the channel is unavailable, never passed. Related: CM-sign (no hard edge). (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22 (D-RA-Q3/Q4): not on the minimal path; Q4 (operator key) is UNANSWERED: ask before claiming. Recommended default applies.
data.title: Signed approvals (L4), later and optional: ssh-keygen -Y sign/verify over the canonical payload against [approvals].signers, verified offline

data.body:
Depends on the probe's verdict; implements only what it CONFIRMED. The ddflow server issues elicitation during the agent's ask call, records via=elicitation; the transcript variant is off by default, T2 only, labelled attested-by-transcript. Touches the MCP server only through a small hook; coordinates with tool-diet leases. (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22 (D-RA-Q5): transcript-attested AskUserQuestion is enabled by default for T2, never T3; verify through hook/transcript attestation; inert in cloud sessions until RA-probe-harness.

The MVP core. operator_gate(verb, params, caller, approval_id): person at terminal as today; agent with an approval recomputes the digest from current state, checks requester, expiry, uses, level, spends one use under the log lock (ask.consumed) and stamps the effect with human, proxy, ask id, level, channel; otherwise refuses naming the route and (auto_request) files the ask. Sites: approval.grant, grants.add, reviewer_trust, gate_accept, api/chore, api/gates failed-review skip, export ack/disable/enable. Also fixes the verdict trusting self-reported human/coded (research Finding 1) for levels above L1. Shared --approval flag helper. (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22 (D-RA-Q2/Q7/Q9/Q12): relayed consent kept one more release with a doctor warning per use then require_approval on; gated acts add forced complete and forced claim only; 1h use window, one use; auto_request on.

Per D-RA-4. Ships examples OFF: review_round up to 5 when the tree changed after triage; skip of a gate whose reviewer was unavailable 3 times; accept measured baseline-red partial. Policy answers are ask.answered by=policy:<id>, policy=true, human=false; consumed only for verbs that allow policy. Company floors only tighten; an agent surface cannot write [approvals]. (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22 (D-RA-Q8): three example rules, ALL OFF, ambiguous operator answer (lead to confirm).

New package ddflow/services/approvals/. sites.py declares one row per verb (gate.skip.failed_review, grant.add, approve.partial, reviewers.approve, chore.approve, export.ack, config.reviewer_command, upgrade.self, plan.confirm, claim.force, complete.force, skew.override) with tier T1/T2/T3, default min level, which state is digested. The test greps ddflow/ for agent_marker/AP.refusal/is_agent uses and fails for one not listed (r-reuse-core, no second list). (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22 (D-RA-Q7): add forced complete and forced claim as T2 sites; others stay ungated.

Operator guide with the threat-model limits stated plainly (research section 3 and 5). (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

Amended 2026-10-22: document the honest limits in the decision doc (chat forgeable with connector token; harness caveats; T3 as L1 on single uid). RA-channel-signed is optional and not awaited.
